You are resolving an in-progress git merge in treams-rs (branch claude/treams-rs-improvements-snetmh). The merge brings in commit 701b5be (condensed into 8251007) ("PB3": a Python test-suite restructuring of the API/adapter/workflow tests) on top of the integration branch, which already contains "PA3" (framework-adapter source changes plus NEW regression tests that PA3 added to the adapter test files). Conflicted files: tests/test_api.py, tests/test_framework_physics.py (large), tests/test_invariants.py, tests/test_support.py, tests/test_torch.py. Do not abort the merge.

Goal: a resolution that preserves BOTH sides' intent:

  • Keep PB3's restructuring (scenario tables, module-scoped engine fixture, exact native-pullback bridge tables, deletions of redundant tests, new invariants).
  • Keep every regression test PA3 added (they guard real fixes: e.g. test_heterogeneous_cluster_scatter_matches_solved_response, test_layer_blocks_follow_interleaved_port_groups, test_port_waves_drive_a_second_system_group_by_group, test_derived_fields_in_a_chiral_exterior_match_normal_api, test_lossless_cross_sections_satisfy_the_optical_theorem, test_declared_record_output_is_checked_in_every_engine, test_framework_physical_mismatches_raise additions, torch read-only/negative-stride constant tests, wrap vector-wave tuple tests, etc.). Inspect git log -p c928b92^2 -- tests/ (condensed into 8251007) (PA3's commits are b1e322e (condensed into 8251007) and its ancestors back to f43174f (condensed into 8251007): git log --oneline f43174f..b1e322e (condensed into 8251007) (condensed into 8251007)) to see exactly what PA3 added to each conflicted file, and git show 701b5be (condensed into 8251007) / git log f43174f..701b5be -- <file> (condensed into 8251007) (condensed into 8251007) for PB3's side. Port PA3's tests into PB3's new structure (e.g. use PB3's engine fixture / helper names), keeping their assertions and tolerances unchanged. Where PB3 deleted a test because it duplicated another, keep the deletion only if the duplicate still exists after the merge; never drop a PA3 regression test.
  • Every test must carry one of the registered category markers (physics, ad_contract, python_contract, public_e2e, oracle_numerical) — there is a guard test (tests/test_suite_contract.py). Use module-level pytestmark or per-test markers consistent with the file.

Verification (all must pass before you commit):

  1. cd treams-rs && just build-ext (the target dir was cleaned; takes a few minutes).
  2. .venv/bin/ruff format tests && .venv/bin/ruff check tests.
  3. uv run --no-sync pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/test_api.py tests/test_framework_physics.py tests/test_invariants.py tests/test_support.py tests/test_torch.py tests/test_jax.py tests/test_advect.py tests/test_suite_contract.py, then the full suite uv run --no-sync pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider (≈4 min) — the full-suite marker guard must pass. Then git add the resolved files and commit the merge with message: "Merge PB3: API, adapter, workflow and docs tests" + a short body explaining how PA3's regression tests were carried into PB3's structure, ending with these two lines: Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 noreply@anthropic.com Claude-Session: [link to a conversation in the cloud] Do NOT push, do not touch other branches or scratch: lanes. Report: how each conflict was resolved, which PA3 tests were ported where, test counts before/after for those files, and the full-suite result.

Result

I resolved the merge and committed it as 5886a6a (condensed into 8251007) "Merge PB3: API, adapter, workflow and docs tests" on claude/treams-rs-improvements-snetmh. Its parents are 4f773f7 (condensed into 8251007) and 701b5be (condensed into 8251007), and the working tree is clean. Nothing was pushed, and no other branches or scratch: lanes were touched.

Verification: all passed.

  • just build-ext: OK.
  • ruff format and ruff check tests: clean.
  • The targeted run (the 8 requested files plus test_adapter_bridges.py): 310 passed, 7 xfailed, 1 xpassed.
  • Full suite: 3362 passed, 36 skipped, 37 xfailed, 1 xpassed in 140 s, exit 0. The marker guard in test_suite_contract passed.
    • The skips are there because matplotlib isn't installed, plus one ufunc case.
    • The one xpass is PB3's own non-strict xfail test_lossless_chiral_slab_conserves_power_at_every_order[jax].

How each conflict was resolved

  • tests/test_api.py: this conflict came from RB1, not PA3. Both sides had deleted test_regular_translation_derivative_at_origin, so only the imports clashed. I took PB3's import of check_pullback, which makes the file identical to PB3's.
  • tests/test_invariants.py: also from RB1. I took PB3's test_translation_position_derivative. It covers every mode pair with l ≤ 3 and |m| ≤ 1, both polarizations and both conventions, including the regular origin at step 1e-6 and tolerances 3e-10/2e-8. That includes every case RB1 had folded into test_translation_position_pullback_on_and_off_axis, at the same tolerances.
  • tests/test_support.py: I kept PB3's test_framework_namespaces_share_one_vocabulary and its catalog fixture. PA3's checks moved into it: every __all__ export (read with ast) must be in the catalog, and the slab signature must start with "(*, basis:". I moved import ast to module level.
    • PB3's deletion of test_documented_sphere_and_recorded_solve stays. The tests it names as replacements, test_api::test_sphere_api_and_optical_theorem and the solve adjoint tests in test_linalg, still exist.
  • tests/test_torch.py: I took PB3's side, which drops _directional and the tests it moved into the bridge table. PA3's read-only/negative-stride constant test and its dtype check for physical constructors survived outside the conflict.
  • tests/test_framework_physics.py: I rebuilt the file from PB3's version (scenarios, module-scoped Engine, _fields) and ported every PA3 test into it (details below). Marker convention follows the file: module-level ad_contract plus one explicit category per test.

Where the PA3 tests went

  • test_framework_physics.py, now using engine.tr, Engine.value_and_grad and Engine.numpy with unchanged assertions and tolerances:
    • test_lossless_cross_sections_satisfy_the_optical_theorem[cluster] (physics)
    • test_parity_cross_sections_require_an_achiral_exterior (python_contract)
    • test_heterogeneous_cluster_scatter_matches_solved_response (public_e2e)
    • test_layer_blocks_follow_interleaved_port_groups (public_e2e)
    • test_port_waves_drive_a_second_system_group_by_group (public_e2e)
    • test_derived_fields_in_a_chiral_exterior_match_normal_api (public_e2e)
    • test_declared_record_output_is_checked_in_every_engine (python_contract)
    • PA3's unknown-polarization check ("positive_helicity or negative_helicity", for both the engine and core) was added to test_framework_physical_mismatches_raise.
  • The two check_direction gradients (interleaved-port slab, second-system port wave) became the scenarios interleaved_slab_thickness and port_wave_second_system. This is how PB3 converted every other check_direction call:
    • Advect is checked against finite differences with the same step and tolerances (1e-5, rtol 2e-5, atol 1e-9).
    • JAX and PyTorch must match Advect at 1e-12.
    • The value is compared with the NumPy namespace at 1e-12.
    • The port-wave test also keeps its direct per-engine value check against core at 1e-12.
  • The torch.wrap vector-wave tuple test lost its _directional helper in PB3. It is now the sph-harm-tuple-gradients case in tests/test_adapter_bridges.py, run for JAX and PyTorch through wrap.
    • This is the one tolerance that changed: the old finite-difference check (rtol 8e-6) became an exact comparison with the native tuple pullback (rtol 1e-13), with the same shape and dtype checks. I did this because the finite-difference check needs the helper PB3 removed, and the native pullback is still finite-difference-checked by test_vectorwaves.
    • The standalone JAX version in test_jax.py is kept.
  • Auto-merged and confirmed intact: the test_advect layer-stack scalar thickness test, the test_jax wrap vector-wave test, the test_testing message and non-finite-imaginary cases, the test_particle_cluster helicity check, and the test_vectorwaves tuple-contract and label-bounds tests.

One thing to know

PB3's commit 7622891 (condensed into 8251007) says the old torch solve common-scale property moved to test_linalg.test_linear_solve_common_scale_invariant. That test doesn't exist on either side, because be8ba5c (condensed into 8251007) (PB2) had already removed it. The property is still covered by the Rust property linear_solve_and_internal_field_amplitude_adjoint and by the bridge table's exact solve cases, and it wasn't a PA3 test, so I kept the deletion. Only PB3's commit message names a location that doesn't exist.

Files changed by the resolution, all under tests/: test_api.py, test_framework_physics.py, test_invariants.py, test_support.py, test_torch.py, test_adapter_bridges.py.
